Annotate pairwise DNA differences with anchored sequence detail

Source: R/geom-alignseq.R
geom_alignseq.Rd

geom_alignseq() draws data prepared by alignseq_data() on annotation panels. In marker mode, all nonmatching events in the selected regions are drawn; contiguous indels have one marker, labelled with their length. Only explicitly selected details windows receive DNA callouts on their respective annotation panels. Nearby windows are merged by the preparation helper.

Usage

geom_alignseq(
  data,
  mapping = NULL,
  mode = c("markers", "rows"),
  size = 2.5,
  family = "mono",
  background = TRUE,
  max_columns = 60,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = FALSE,
  ...,
  sequence_position = c("auto", "left", "center", "right"),
  colour_scheme = c("nucleotide", "difference"),
  difference_colours = c(aligned = "#E6E6E6", mismatch = "#E69F00", indel = "#D73027")
)

Arguments

data

A table returned by alignseq_data(). Must be supplied explicitly. Optional boundary_after (logical) and boundary_label (character) columns mark verified boundaries, such as splice donors, after selected bases in the equally spaced sequence detail. These do not alter the DNA strings.

mapping

Optional aesthetic overrides. Prepared metadata and x/y/track are mapped automatically. Use anchor track names matching the annotation facet, never a link-panel track.

mode

"markers" (default) or "rows". Rows display all selected columns as an equally spaced DNA row in each sequence's own annotation panel, connected to the midpoint of its displayed genomic interval. Row mode requires one contiguous alignment-column selection per sequence.

size

DNA character size in mm.

family

Character font, default "mono".

background

Logical; draw nucleotide backgrounds.

max_columns

Maximum columns in a callout or row view (default 60). Longer windows raise an error requesting a narrower selection.

na.rm, show.legend, ...

Standard layer arguments. Event colours and shapes use the default nucleotide scheme: substitution blue circle, insertion orange triangle, deletion purple inverted triangle, ambiguous grey cross. The difference scheme also uses its palette for substitution and indel markers. No fill scale is added, so existing exon and link palettes remain available.

sequence_position

Horizontal placement of sequence blocks: "auto" (default), "left", "center", or "right". Automatic placement stays near the genomic anchor and moves blocks apart before stacking. Explicit positions keep their horizontal alignment and stack overlapping blocks vertically. Placement is in panel space after genomic scaling, including on reversed panels. Blocks are kept within the available space with room for sequence names, so wide centred blocks may shift right to fit.

colour_scheme

"nucleotide" (default) colours A/C/G/T bases separately. "difference" uses a neutral background for aligned columns, one colour for substitutions, and another for insertions and deletions. Both sequences highlight the same differing alignment columns. Ambiguous IUPAC bases remain neutral rather than being called verified mismatches.

difference_colours

Named character vector of three colours with keys aligned, mismatch, and indel. Used with colour_scheme = "difference". Defaults to grey aligned columns, orange mismatches, and red indels. Text switches between black and white for readable contrast, assuming a white panel background when colours are translucent. With background = FALSE, mismatch and indel colours apply to the letters, while aligned letters retain their neutral grey shade.

Value

A ggplot2 layer using a native annotation geom. Cartesian coordinates are required. In ggexon, use with annotation data and facet_genomics().

Details

Each sequence block has one smooth curved connector from the midpoint of its displayed genomic interval to the bottom centre of the sequence block. Marker and connector anchors follow scale_x_ggexon_genomic() automatically. Callout columns are equally spaced in panel space after genomic scaling: they are schematic alignment detail, not an additional genomic ruler. Each panel displays only its own sequence in the supplied orientation. Markers describe the query relative to the reference, not evolutionary change.

See also

alignseq_data(), geom_exon2(), scale_x_ggexon_genomic()
